entries.claim: VideoRepick reset video can swap visually identical cubes after the demonstrated pickup and placement. The demonstrated cube's initial table location is therefore not necessarily its execution target location; track its continuous motion through the remainder of the video before grounding the first pick.
entries.conditions: When reviewing a VideoRepick reset demonstration, inspect the post-placement interval for cube motion. If a swap appears in sparse samples, narrow to dense chronological views to preserve identity, then ground on the current original front image. Recompute identity every episode; this does not imply all demonstrations contain a swap.

entries.claim: A correctly grounded VideoRepick cube can still be approached incorrectly by the VLA: in a crowded array, an unguarded100-control first-pick budget ended with the gripper over an adjacent cube and the next candidate proposing closure. Review visual target alignment before near-table descent rather than letting the full-phase duration prior stand in for correct targeting.
entries.conditions: First pickup in crowded arrays with adjacent cubes, especially before actual grasp alignment has been visually verified. Keep ordinary high approach separate from final descent/grasp: consider an initial70-control review, then <=16-control close review if alignment is uncertain, or explicitly install a before-command gripper guard until the intended cube is confirmed between fingers. The guard observes closure proposals, not object identity or collisions, and70 is not a demonstrated safe bound. Evidence: authorized100 controls at199; earliest sampled alignment warning256 (+57), dense284-299 confirms wrong-target descent; exact onset remains uncertain. Recovery was possible before any visible wrong-object grasp. A guarded50-control recovery authorization woke after32 before closure; correct lift followed30 more controls.
